trend_source: This US TikTok listing five expensive things 'worth the money' pulled 843.6k views and 191.1k likes, proving people love reframing spending as a value decision rather than guilt.

Cheap can cost you more later. Here are the pricey buys I never regret.
I stopped feeling guilty about spending on these five things.
talking_points: Good shoes and a reliable phone you use daily beat five cheap replacements over the year
Health screening and dental you actually keep up with, so small problems stay small
Protection you set up young, because premiums generally reflect your age and health when you start
Time-saving spends that let you earn or rest, not lifestyle inflation for show

why_it_works: It borrows a proven, non-preachy angle that celebrates smart spending instead of shaming it, which keeps viewers watching.

trend_source: A US personal finance creator's rule-of-thumb video (rent x0.3, car x5, invest x300) drew 541.3k views and 34k likes, proving simple multipliers travel.

hooks: Four quick multipliers told me if I was overspending in about 30 seconds.
Grab your monthly pay. These four numbers reveal your real money picture.
I ran my life through four simple ratios and it changed my next big purchase.

Car: in SG factor in COE, so run the total cost, not just the sticker
Freedom number: a rough target of what you would need invested to stop relying on a paycheck, using a conservative withdrawal assumption
Guilt-free fund: a small planned slice you can enjoy without derailing goals

why_it_works: Rules of thumb are highly saveable and shareable, and adapting them for COE and CPF makes it genuinely local rather than copied.
how_to_film: On-screen text for each multiplier as you say it. Fast pace, one rule per line. Open on the hook while holding up a phone calculator.
